findings.title: The spec delta contradicts itself: one button per change vs. buttons left out; back required on a computer that has none
The change group's overflow clips the change buttons' focus ring
findings.scoreReason: The claim holds: the global ring (2px outline, 2px offset) sits outside a button as tall as the clipped `height: var(--tap)` group, so keyboard users on a computer lose the ring this change added. But it is a one-line fix (an inset outline-offset on `.wv-change`), so do it now or mention it in the final comment rather than open an item.

findings.title: Change buttons wrapped to the hidden line stay focusable and exposed to assistive technology
findings.scoreReason: The claim is right, but it only matters when a keyboard or screen-reader user has a header narrow enough to wrap the buttons, which is rare on a panel used mostly by touch. A fix needs JS to measure the row and mark buttons inert, which costs more than the problem is worth.

findings.title: No taskPercent case tells rounding down from rounding to nearest
findings.scoreReason: `taskProgress` calls `taskPercent` (shared/change-progress.ts:17), so the existing `changeLine` case 2/3 → «66 %» would already fail if the function rounded to nearest. The extra case adds no protection.

findings.title: Say 'narrow header' as line 74 does, not 'on the phone'

escapes.reason: The window header's buttons never shrink; the folder button left no room on a phone, so the header overflowed and widened the page
